points.title: Do You Want to Build a Snowman?
points.kid: Anna knocks and knocks for years. Why doesn't Elsa ever open the door?
points.parent: Repair-arc reading: the closed door is armor, not rejection — Elsa believes staying away IS the loving thing. Both sisters are hurting on opposite sides of the same door, each thinking the other doesn't want them. Worth asking: has anyone ever seemed to shut you out when they were really protecting you?

options.reply: She loves her the WHOLE time — watch her face on the other side of the door.

options.text: She's scared of hurting Anna again
options.reply: YES. The door is armor around an old accident. Protection that outlived its moment — Moana's dad has the same rule about the reef.
This is years before she's queen. It started the night of the accident.

quiz.question: Why does Elsa keep the door closed?

points.title: Anna comes to the palace
points.kid: Anna climbs a whole frozen mountain to reach her sister. What makes her keep going?
points.parent: Repair-arc: this is the RETURN step — going toward the person instead of away. Notice it doesn't work yet: Anna returns, but leads with the problem (the frozen kingdom), and Elsa's armor slams down harder. Return alone isn't enough; the truth step hasn't happened yet. Real repairs often take more than one try.

options.text: Anna doesn't really want to fix things
options.reply: She climbed a MOUNTAIN for this. Wanting isn't the problem.

options.text: Elsa's fear rises faster than Anna's words can land
options.reply: YES. When armor is threatened it strikes out — Elsa literally storms. You can't reason with armor; the hurt under it has to be spoken to. First tries at repair often fail. Keep watching.
Olaf is actually the most honest one on that mountain!

quiz.question: Anna reaches Elsa at last — why does it go wrong?

points.title: Anna's choice
points.kid: Anna could run to her kiss and save herself. She turns toward Elsa instead. Why?
points.parent: The whole repair arc lands here. Anna's act says the truth out loud better than words: you are worth standing in front of. And watch what it unlocks — Elsa finally learns the counter-rule to the one she was raised on: not conceal-don't-feel, but love as the thing that makes power safe. Repair that re-equips, exactly like Te Fiti restoring Maui's hook.

options.reply: Ouch — the movie has other plans for Hans.
Close guess — the movie WANTS you to think that. But Anna never reaches him...

options.text: Anna putting herself between the sword and Elsa
options.reply: YES. The act of true love isn't received — it's GIVEN, by the person we thought needed saving. Love turned outward, not a kiss arriving.

quiz.question: What is the act of true love that saves the day?

points.title: The gates stay open
points.kid: At the end, Elsa makes an ice rink for everyone and the gates stay open. What changed — her powers, or something else?
points.parent: Her powers are identical in the first scene and the last. What changed is the rule she lives by — fear says conceal, love says connect. Master lesson, same as Moana's father: who you are is a choice, not a fixed thing, and the people around you can change their rules too. Closing couch question: is there a door in our family that could open a little more?
